nodes.name: Webhook: Triage
nodes.notes: POST {ticket_id, customer_email, subject?, message, channel?}. Replies once, after the ticket is resolved or escalated.

nodes.name: CONFIG
nodes.notes: THE SETTINGS NODE. Language model, service URLs, safety limits (confidence, iterations, keywords, reply mode). See the Read Me First note and the README.

nodes.name: Agent Playbook
nodes.notes: THE OTHER NODE YOU MAY EDIT. The prompts and the agent's tools (add a tool = add one entry). Checked on every run; see 02-agentic-support-triage-EXTEND.md.

nodes.name: Plan Ticket
nodes.notes: Checks auth (optional), CONFIG, and the ticket. Also screens the text for sensitive keywords (SENSITIVE_KEYWORDS): a deterministic safety net that does not depend on the language model noticing.

nodes.name: Respond Early
nodes.notes: Replies to tickets that stop early: 400, 401, 500, replays of a finished ticket (200), in-progress duplicates (409), state store down (503).

nodes.name: Claim Ticket
nodes.notes: POST /tickets/{id}/claim {ttl_seconds} -> 200 {claimed, record:{status, result?}}. ATOMIC: exactly one concurrent delivery gets claimed:true. This replaces check-then-mark, which let two simultaneous deliveries both run the whole agent.

nodes.name: Claim Verdict
nodes.notes: Claimed -> go. Already finished -> replay the stored result. Someone else is working on it -> 409. State store unreachable -> 503 (we cannot promise to run it only once).

nodes.name: Classify Ticket
nodes.notes: ENGINE (protected). Keyword screen, then the model classifies the ticket, then the gates that send it to a human before the agent runs: sensitive, low confidence, always-escalate categories. A model outage here is its own stage (classifier), not a fake sensitive ticket.

nodes.name: Needs Agent?
nodes.notes: continue -> the agent runs. Anything else -> straight to a human.

nodes.name: Run Agent
nodes.notes: ENGINE (protected). The bounded ReAct loop and the generic tool engine: validates inputs, URL-encodes ids, enforces ownership (owner_field), verified-order rules and the refund guard, step limit, time budget, answer cap. The tools and prompts come from the Agent Playbook node, so adding a tool does not mean editing this node.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { to: $('Plan Ticket').first().json.ticket.customer_email, subject: 'Re: ' + $('Plan Ticket').first().json.ticket.subject, body: $('Run Agent').first().json.answer, idempotency_key: 'ticket:' + $('Plan Ticket').first().json.ticket.ticket_id } }}

nodes.name: Send Customer Reply
nodes.notes: POST {EMAIL_API_URL}/send {to, subject, body, idempotency_key}. Best effort: the answer is also in the response body, and a failed send is reported.

nodes.name: Reply Verdict
nodes.notes: Builds the "resolved" response, and what is stored for replays (without the tool trail). A failed reply send is reported, not hidden.

nodes.name: Prepare Escalation
nodes.notes: Builds the helpdesk ticket: the customer's message, why it was escalated, the classification, the draft reply if there is one, and the agent's trail.

nodes.name: Create Helpdesk Ticket
nodes.notes: POST /tickets {ticket_id, customer_email, subject, priority, tag, description} -> 2xx created, or 409 if that ticket_id already exists (also fine). One retry on transient failure.

nodes.name: Helpdesk Transient?
nodes.notes: One more try for a transient failure.

nodes.name: Create Helpdesk Ticket (retry)
nodes.notes: The one retry.

nodes.name: Escalation Verdict
nodes.notes: Created (or already existed) -> 200 escalated. Helpdesk unreachable -> 502 escalation_failed, the claim is released so the sender's retry runs again, and ops is told. (The original said "escalated" and marked the ticket done even when no helpdesk ticket existed.)

nodes.name: Outcome Recorded?
nodes.notes: Success -> store the result for replays. Failure -> release the claim so a retry is allowed.

nodes.name: Complete Ticket
nodes.notes: POST /tickets/{id}/complete {status:"resolved"|"escalated", result} -> 200. Later deliveries of this ticket get the stored result.

nodes.name: Release Ticket
nodes.notes: POST /tickets/{id}/release -> 200. Lets a retry of a failed escalation run again.

nodes.name: Finish
nodes.notes: Collects the final response and any alerts (including a state store that would not take the result or release).

nodes.name: Respond Final
nodes.notes: The single reply for a ticket that was worked on.

nodes.name: Expand Notifications
nodes.notes: Runs AFTER the reply. One Slack message per notice (escalations, failures). Nothing if Slack is not configured. Text is escaped.

nodes.name: Send Slack Alert
nodes.notes: Slack-compatible incoming webhook. A failed alert is ignored on purpose.

parameters.content:
## Agentic Support Triage
**Setup (about 10 minutes)**
1. Run the backing services (a reference implementation is included: `node 02-agentic-support-triage-mock-server.js`, port 5000). It contains a **scripted stand-in for the language model**, not a real one.
2. Open **CONFIG**: point `LLM_API_URL` / `CHAT_MODEL` at an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint (`/v1/chat/completions`), set the order, knowledge-base, refund, helpdesk, email and ticket-state URLs, and optionally `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`.
3. To change the agent's wording or add a tool, edit **Agent Playbook** (see 02-agentic-support-triage-EXTEND.md); the nodes marked ENGINE enforce the safety rules and normally never need editing.
4. Review the safety settings: `REPLY_MODE` (`send` emails the agent's answer; `draft` sends it to a human instead), `CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD`, `SENSITIVE_KEYWORDS`, `ALWAYS_ESCALATE_CATEGORIES`, `MAX_ITERATIONS`.
5. Activate. Send `POST /webhook/support/triage` with `{"ticket_id":"T-1","customer_email":"a@b.co","subject":"...","message":"..."}`.

**Each ticket:** claim it (atomic) -> keyword screen -> classify -> bounded agent (own-orders-only tools) -> reply to the customer, or escalate to the helpdesk with the full trail -> store the result -> alert ops.
